{{Short description|Zero-sum game where competitions between strategies contain a cycle}}
An '''intransitive''' or '''non-transitive game''' is a [[Zero-sum game|zero-sum]] game in which pairwise competitions between the strategies contain a cycle. If strategy A beats strategy B, B beats C, and C beats A, then the binary relation "to beat" is intransitive, since transitivity would require that A beat C. The terms "transitive game" or "intransitive game" are not used in [[game theory]].

A prototypical example of an intransitive game is the game [[rock, paper, scissors]]. In [[probability|probabilistic]] games like [[Penney's game]], the violation of transitivity results in a more subtle way, and is often presented as a probability [[paradox]].
